headline: Record fees and wider margins power strong quarter
summary_short: State Street reported Q3 2026 EPS of $3.69 (+33% y/y) on total revenue of $4.0B (+13%), with ROTCE of 25.1% and a pre-tax margin of 34.6%.
summary_long: Total revenue rose 13% y/y to $4.0B as fee revenue grew 11% and net interest income 21%. Servicing fees rose 10%, management fees 20% and FX trading services 17%, on record FX client volumes. Expenses rose 8% on revenue-related costs and strategic investment, giving positive operating leverage of 531 basis points. Net income was $1.09B. AUC/A reached a record $59.2T and AUM $6.3T. CET1 was 11.0%. State Street returned $651M to common shareholders, including $400M of buybacks, and won its first Wealth Services mandate.
confidence_notes: All deltas are the release's own stated y/y and q/q changes, rounded to whole percent where the release does so. The release reports no notable items in 3Q26, 2Q26 or 3Q25, so GAAP and ex-notables results coincide. ROTCE is a non-GAAP measure as defined by the company. The release states no numeric forward guidance.

drivers.explanation: The CEO cites record servicing and management fees and record FX client volumes, and the eleventh straight quarter of positive operating leverage excluding notable items.
Higher fee revenue and net interest income; servicing fees up 10%, management fees up 20%, FX trading services up 17%, partly offset by 29% lower other fee revenue on market-related adjustments.
Reflects a 16 basis point increase in net interest margin versus a year ago; flat versus Q2 as a higher day count offset a 1 basis point NIM decline.
Net income rose 27% on revenue growth outpacing the 8% rise in expenses.
Increase mainly due to higher market levels, net new business and flows.
